title: KronLSTM: Kronecker Delta Rule for Linear Attention

beats.text: Before you train your next model, see how KronLSTM cuts +8.3% of memory overhead.
beats.visual_focus: A neural matrix flickering and fading into static.

beats.text: The villain is the Delta Rule. It updates the entire matrix blindly, overwriting vital context like a sledgehammer in a library.
KronLSTM pivots to the Kronecker Delta Rule. It performs surgical updates, modifying memory only along a single, precise vector direction.
beats.visual_focus: A laser beam cutting through a matrix with surgical precision.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—calling out memory corruption in linear attention models is exactly the kind of pain point I actually care about. I didn't swipe because you didn't waste time with a 'Hey guys' intro. However, in Beat 3, the phrasing 'along a single. Precise vector direction' felt a bit clunky and grammatically weird, which made me pause for a second to figure out if you meant a rank-1 update or something else. Otherwise, the performance stats in Beat 5 actually felt grounded and not like marketing fluff.
